caption: Duty factor sets the average exposure. In one averaging window, SSB voice averages about a fifth of PEP while keyed, CW about two-fifths, and constant-carrier FT8 runs at full PEP - and each mode is keyed only half the window - so the same 100 watt PEP radio averages roughly 10, 20, and 50 watts. Exposure is judged on the average, so a lower duty factor permits higher power for the same exposure.
spoken: The top panel shows a 60-second averaging window with three timelines. For SSB voice the key is down half the window but speech averages only about a fifth of peak envelope power, for about 10 percent average. CW is keyed half the time at about two-fifths average power, for about 20 percent. FT8 transmits a continuous carrier on alternate 15-second slots, for about 50 percent. The bottom panel bars the results - SSB near 10 percent, CW 20, FT8 50, and a continuous FM or RTTY carrier at 100 - making the point that the same PEP produces very different averages, and a lower duty factor means more headroom under the exposure limits.
